DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine) is the standard for medical imaging data.

Loading DICOM volumes requires parsing specific tags (PixelSpacing, SliceThickness, RescaleSlope) and handling the coordinate system differences between DICOM (patient-centered, middle-of-voxel) and typical graphics APIs (corner-of-voxel).
This method bridges that gap, enabling accurate volume rendering of medical data.
It is commonly used in medical visualization software, research prototypes, and clinical PACS viewers.
